title: Handoff chronicle and signal gates — release timing & telemetry playpad
content:
Context / intent:
This is my personal handoff note for the upcoming model flip (v2.1 -> v2.2-quant). Goal: make the rollout frictionless between product, SDK, and SRE, and ensure telemetry signal gates are explicit and actionable. Use this as the single scratchpad for on-call handoff, tiny-runbook excerpts, and questions to resolve before we open traffic.

Audience: on-call SRE, release owner (Raya), SDK lead (Samir), PM (Ibrahim).

High-level plan (one-liner):
- Night-window deploy, phased traffic steps (0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%), SDK pin for client cohorts, observe 30m at each step with auto-until-fix guardrails.

Prereqs before I sign off to open traffic:
- All canaries pass (unit/integration smoke) — PR #988 green with e2e mocks
- Benchmark slab: p50 <= 320ms, p95 <= 1.2s for baseline query mix (seq_len 64/256) on dedicated pool
- Memory delta < 5% (KV-cache warmup verified)
- Canary cohort (internal tenants) configured in SDK toggle list (cohort ids: C-INT-A, C-INT-B)
- Emergency rollback route configured (routing rule id: route-rollback-2025-10-14)
- Observability dashboards loaded in console (quick links below)

Quick links (load these in parallel at each step):
- Console dashboard: console.redwood/model/v2.2-quant/overview
- Latency histogram (p50/p90/p95): console.redwood/latency/hist/v2.2-quant
- Error budget burn: console.redwood/errors/eb/v2.2-quant
- Cost per token estimate run: docs/cost-estimates/v2.2-quant
- Linear ticket: RED-4123

Traffic step checklist (operational):
- Step 0.1% (priming):
  - Duration: min 30m, target 30–90m
  - Observe: p50, p95, error rate, timeouts, rate-limited responses, model-specific rejections
  - Telemetry gates (if any tripped -> pause):
    - error rate > baseline + 0.25% (absolute) OR 3x baseline relative
    - p95 > baseline p95 * 1.6
    - spike in 5xx or grpc UNAVAILABLE > 0.2%
    - client-observed content deviation alerts (see quality probes below)
  - On success: move to 1% after approval from release owner (Slack ack)

- Step 1% (confidence):
  - Duration: 30–60m
  - Add: sample-based quality checks (synthetic prompt set): run diff-tester job against both versions every 10m
  - Additional gates:
    - new_alerts_for_prompt_flips > 10 in 30m -> pause
    - tokens/second delta > 2x baseline -> investigate batching regressions

- Step 5% (stress):
  - Duration: 60m minimum
  - Monitor: per-tenant latency distribution, client-side tail latency (SDK telemetry), memory footprint by host
  - Gate: host OOMs, eviction events, KV-cache misses > baseline + 10% -> stop and collect heap profiles

- Step 20% -> 100%
  - Progression conservative; allow time to fix infra issues, but can accelerate if stable after 3x step windows.

Quality probes (quick and dirty):
- Probe corpus: 120 prompts derived from high-confidence failing signatures in last 30 days (sensitive truncation, hallucination-prone examples, and safety edgecases). Run 50-sample checks per step.
- Metric: semantic-stability-score (synthetic baseline from v2.1). If semantic-stability drops below 92% -> immediate pause.
- Automated diff tester: runs in CI and posts summary to #deploy-flips (Slack). If > 6 prompts flip category (OK->fail or fail->OK) in 30m -> manual review.

Signal sources and owners (who watches what):
- SRE (Samir): infra metrics, p95/p99 latency, host OOMs, queue lengths, autoscaler behavior
- SDK (Raya): client-side error rates, tokenization mismatches, SDK pin toggles correctness
- Product (Ibrahim): semantic regressions, safety alerts, customer-facing anomalies
- Observability (Harper): dashboard snapshots, delta comparisons, runbook excerpts

Handoff notes (for on-call):
- If you see a sustained latency p95 > 1.5s or error rate > 1% sustained for 10m, hit the route-rollback-2025-10-14 flag (CLI: infractl route set route-rollback-2025-10-14 --active true) and notify #deploy-flips with subject: "ROLLBACK: v2.2-quant - <metric>"
- If memory trends upward past 75% host utilization across the pool, throttle new cohorts and schedule heap profile collection (script: tools/heap-collect.sh --pool quant-v2 --window 600)
- For content regressions, run diff tool: tools/diff-tester --baseline v2.1 --candidate v2.2-quant --samples 50 --out /tmp/diff.json then ping Raya + Product Lead with the summary.

Unresolved questions / TODOs before full rollout (my items):
- Add alert that correlates client-SDK sentinel errors with server 5xx spikes (Signal correlation alert) — assigned to Samir (RED-4207)
- Validate SDK pin logic across mobile prod vs web prod (edge-case: mobile uses older SDK; need safe fallback) — Samir + Raya to confirm by EOD before step 1%
- Confirm billing tag propagation for quantized model so cost dashboards show accurate per-token cost (Finance flagged discrepancies last time)
- Decide on canary cohort length for enterprise tenants: 72h vs 24h (tradeoff: coverage vs time-to-fix). Product preference: 72h for top 20 tenants.

Post-mortem triggers (auto-create PMR if any of these happen):
- Any silent data loss incident or tenant-visible corrupted output
- Major incident (SEV1) during rollout window
- >10% customers affected by latency/error regressions for >4h

Quick commands cheatsheet (useful during noise):
- route rollback: infractl route set route-rollback-2025-10-14 --active true
- pin cohort toggle (SDK): sdk-admin cohort pin --cohort C-INT-A --model v2.2-quant
- sample diff run (local): tools/diff-tester --baseline v2.1 --candidate v2.2-quant --samples 50
- snapshot logs (last 30m): infractl logs --service model-serving --since 30m --out /tmp/logs.tgz

Communication plan (who says what where):
- Step openings and moves: release owner posts to #deploy-flips with step, timestamp, quick metric snapshot (p50/p95, error rate)
- Any pause/rollback: release owner calls SRE pager and posts short summary in #deploy-flips; SRE on-call takes lead for rollback ops
- Post-rollout summary: short writeup in Confluence + deploy retrospective invite in calendar (1h async + 30m sync for top issues)

Notes to self (observational heuristics):
- Cold-start penalties for quantized v2.2 show in first 20m on new hosts — expect p95 to transiently increase by ~120ms while KV warms
- Autoscaler behavior tuned aggressively: if we see repeat scale-up/scale-down cycles, increase cooldown and cap to reduce thrash
- Prefer manual step approval for 5%->20% transition when there are concurrent infra anomalies (less automated risk)

End-of-doc checklist before I hand this to Raya:
- [ ] Confirm hooks to route rollback are reachable from runbook scripts
- [ ] Finalize probe corpus (review with PM)
- [ ] Ensure Linear tickets referenced are updated with step decisions
- [ ] Slack shortplay message template drafted for release owner

If anything goes sideways during the window: keep notes in this doc (timestamped), capture dashboard snapshots, and do not hesitate to hit rollback.

---
Timestamped scratch entry: 2025-10-20 22:14 — observed a 0.3% increase in tokenization mismatches during internal canary priming; probable cause: subtle tokenizer version bump in mobile SDK. Action: pin mobile cohorts out of rollout, create SDK patch PR to align tokenizer, target hotfix before public 1% step.
